name: Ngojama
body:
NGOJAMA
CR 6

This brown-skinned person looks nearly human, save for the small horns crowning its head and the iron spikes extending from the palms of its hands.

XP 2,400
CE Medium outsider (chaotic, evil, native)
Init +4; Senses darkvision 120 ft., scent; Perception +12

DEFENSE

AC 27 AC 18, touch 14, flat-footed 14 (+4 Dex, +4 natural)
hp 68 (8d10+24)
Fort +9, Ref +10, Will +5; Immune charm, fear

OFFENSE

Speed 60 ft., climb 30 ft.
Melee 2 palm spikes +8 (1d8+2)
Special Attacks blood drinking, rend (2 palm spikes, 2d6+6)

STATISTICS

Str 18, Dex 18, Con 16, Int 15, Wis 13, Cha 15
Base Atk +8; CMB +12; CMD 26
Feats Iron Will, Lunge, Stealthy, Weapon Focus (palm spikes)
Skills Acrobatics +12, Bluff +13, Climb +20, Escape Artist +6, Intimidate +10, Perception +12, Sense Motive +12, Stealth +17, Survival +9
Languages Abyssal, Common
SQ carnivore, difficult to control, water aversion

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Blood Drinking (Su)

When a ngojama rends a creature, it regains hit points equal to the damage dealt. Additionally, targets struck become fatigued. (If they are fatigued already, they become exhausted instead) (DC 17 Fort negates fatigue) The save DC is Constitution-based.

Carnivore (Ex)

The ngojama has +5 on Survival checks when using its scent to track any creatures with living flesh.

Difficult to Control (Ex)

As a swift action each turn, the ngojama can reroll the initial save to end any mind-affecting spell on it.

Water Aversion (Ex)

A ngojama cannot swim and will not voluntarily cross or step into water.

The ngojama is a fiendish creature that haunts dark forests; it is almost human in appearance except for two horns on their head and multiple iron like spikes jutting from their palms that they use to impale their prey; because of these spikes, ngojama can never use handheld tools.

Ngojama are aggressive and fearless, using their keen senses to track down and maul prey. They then take delight in tracking and ambushing humanoids out in the wilderness and mauling them. Never one to pass up their favorite meal, they have been known to drain the blood of a target or even consume their flesh.

While difficult to control, some evil spellcasters have tried to entreat one to assassinate a target. Woe betide any caster who forces the ngojama to do their bidding; for the ngojama will bear a grudge against the caster until it can exact its vengeance.
